solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: President not brought back after laundering

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the laundering word in the answer

parts.note: laundering clothes is washing them

indicators.note: brought back says the little word not is to be read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: A leader who is unexpectedly not recalled once a money-laundering scandal breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' gives the three letters that 'after' places at the end; George Washington was the first US president.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first US head of state, so a president is a fair description of him.

clue.text: Some guests, rowdy when turning up: most bad!

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the hidden run is read bottom to top, backwards
some of the letters of the words guests and rowdy are taken, a run hidden across them

explanation.surface: A rowdy bunch of party guests arriving: the worst kind of evening for a host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes TSROW from guesTS ROWdy; 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Worst is the superlative of bad, the same meaning as the phrase most bad.

clue.text: Striking power shown by shire horse

indicators.note: shown by places the striking word next to the county, so the county comes first

parts.note: a shire is an English county, here Suffolk in East Anglia
punch is the force of a blow, striking power

explanation.surface: A heavy shire horse displays its formidable kicking strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is a county of eastern England; the Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught horse. 'shire horse' wants to be the definition, but Shire is a different breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk Punch is a chestnut breed of heavy draught horse from East Anglia.

clue.text: Russian, perhaps: one seen at the front

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the van is the leading part, the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A Russian soldier glimpsed leading the charge at the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name, so a Russian man may be one, signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Friendly girl goes about eastern part of UK

indicators.note: goes about says the girl word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
NI, Northern Ireland, is one of the parts of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A sociable girl travels around the east of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial and friendly are synonyms, both meaning warm and pleasant in manner.

clue.text: Old relative to remove occasionally

parts.note: a nan is a grandmother, a relative
to doff a hat is to remove it

explanation.surface: An elderly relative is being told to take something off.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on and off means doing it intermittently, now and then, from time to time.

clue.text: Artist's retirement involved collecting silver

indicators.note: collecting says the reworked letters gather the silver symbol inside them
involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters of retirement are reworked

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A painter whose retirement was spent collecting silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges RETIREMENT into RENEMRITTE, and 'collecting' takes AG into it; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Virginia perhaps guards posh item of sculpture

indicators.note: guards says the state word surrounds and protects the posh letter

parts.note: Virginia is an example of a US state
U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: Virginia keeps watch over a smart piece of sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' puts U inside STATE. U meaning upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, a standard piece of sculpture.

clue.text: Match official before shower repeated lines

indicators.note: before puts the official first, ahead of the weather word

parts.note: ref is short for referee, the official in charge of a match
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A referee stepping into the shower after the game, singing the same lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the chorus of a song or poem, the lines that recur in each verse.

clue.text: Expert regularly handles physical training

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word handles

explanation.surface: A specialist routinely runs the PE sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a skilled person, a synonym for an expert.

clue.text: Perhaps saw stolen goods returned

indicators.note: returned says the word for stolen goods is read backwards

parts.note: loot is plunder, stolen goods

explanation.surface: A witness may have seen stolen goods being handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses LOOT. 'saw' is the noun for a cutting tool, not the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of a hand tool, which perhaps signals.

clue.text: Most robust male deer crossing different side

indicators.note: crossing says the deer word spans across the reworked letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a hart is an adult male deer

indicators.note: different says the letters of side are put in another order

explanation.surface: The toughest stag crosses to the far side of the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' gives DIES, held by the stag in a 'crossing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiest is the superlative of hardy, meaning tough and able to endure, so most robust.

clue.text: Portable shelter housing Geordie and me becomes family residence

indicators.note: housing says the shelter word contains the other letters

parts.note: a tent is a shelter that can be carried and pitched anywhere
Geordies come from Newcastle, in the north-east of England, NE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A camping tent that holds a Newcastle native and the speaker turns into the family home.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne, in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into flats where families live, a residence.

clue.text: Cook finally coming in cooked lean joint

indicators.note: coming in says the last letter enters the reworked letters
cooked means altered or fiddled, so the letters of lean are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of the word Cook

explanation.surface: A chef arrives at last to prepare a lean cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges LEAN into ANLE, and 'coming in' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint linking the foot and the leg.

clue.text: Class of steamship in new rota

indicators.note: in says the steamship letters sit inside the reworked letters
new says the letters of rota are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Crew grading the classes of a steamship on a fresh duty roster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives AORT, opened by 'in' to take the ship letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To class things is to sort them into groups, which is what the verb assort means.

clue.text: Celebrity holds right shape

indicators.note: holds says the renown word contains the right letter

parts.note: celebrity in the sense of renown is fame

explanation.surface: A famous person keeps in good physical shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts R inside FAME. 'Celebrity' means the quality of being famous, not a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame is a person's body or build, as in a slight frame, hence their shape.

clue.text: Son loses ball on long grass

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the son remnant above, before the longing word
loses says the ball letter is removed from the word son

parts.note: taken as written
O is round, like a ball
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A boy mislays his ball in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' drops O from SON to leave SN. 'grass' is the verb meaning inform, not turf.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone is British slang for informing on them, the same as to snitch.

clue.text: Dish fried quickly starts to reduce, needing extra wine

parts.note: a sauté is a dish of food fried quickly in a little fat

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of the words reduce, needing and extra

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: once the pan-fried dish starts to reduce, add more wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes R, N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Daughter with strange musical instrument

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned British word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A girl takes up an unusual instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM meaning odd is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is a percussion instrument played by striking a skin stretched over a frame.

clue.text: Copy poem written in 1050

indicators.note: written in says the poem is put inside the Roman numerals

parts.note: 1050 in Roman numerals is M for 1000 and L for 50
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A scribe transcribes a poem composed in the eleventh century.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy something is to imitate it, which is one sense of the verb model, as in modelling oneself on a hero.

clue.text: Struggle with wife's opinion

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle for something

explanation.surface: A man battles with his wife's point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a way of seeing a matter, a belief or opinion.

clue.text: What scouts do about centre of local church

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letter of the word local

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Scouts wonder what to do around the middle of the village church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes C from loCal. A recce, short for reconnaissance, is British informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Military scouts carry out reconnaissance, a recce, to explore territory ahead.

clue.text: Winding West Indies street crossed by Edward

indicators.note: crossed by says the name lies across the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A meandering Caribbean road that a man named Edward walks across.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisted means full of bends and turns, the same as winding.

clue.text: Driving in a fast race, cut part of foot

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the fast motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
to hew is to cut, as with an axe
the heel is the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: A racer at speed injures part of a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at the wheel is in the driver's seat, steering, so driving.
